title: SA/189/2019 of RAMZAN Vs GAFFAR( DECEASED)

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Second Appeal No. 189 of 2019
Ramzan
 ...Plaintiff/Appellant
Vs.
Gaffar (Deceased) and Others
...Defendants/Respondents
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the appellant.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J (Oral)
This is a second appeal, which has been preferred by the
plaintiff/appellant, challenging the concurrent judgments impugned,
dated 26.05.2015 as rendered by Civil Judge (J.D.), Vikasnagar,
District Dehradun in Original Suit No. 536 of 2007 'Shri Ramzan vs.
Gaffar and Others', whereby, the suit of the plaintiff/appellant for
grant of decree of permanent injunction has been dismissed, which
later on, on a challenge being given in the civil appeal being Civil
Appeal No. 34 of 2016 'Shri Ramzan vs. Gaffar and Others' has also
been dismissed on 03.08.2019, thereby concurrently dismissing the
suit, which was preferred by the plaintiff/appellant before the learned
court below in relation to the property described at the foot of the
plaint, which constituted to be a land lying in Khasra No. 56 having
an area of 0.700 hectare situated in Mauja Matak Majri Pargana
Pachwadoon, Tehsil Vikasnagar, District Dehradun. The boundaries
of the property were more particularly described as to be, in the east
land of Madan Pal, in the west-land of Gram Samaj and plaintiff, in
the north- land of Haseena and plaintiff, in the south- Government
canal.
2. In the relation to the aforesaid disputed property, the Suit,
which was instituted by the plaintiff (appellant herein) on 31.07.2007
was for a grant of decree of permanent injunction as against the
defendants, their agents and representatives, or any one claiming
under them may be injuncted from forcefully interfering over the
Khasra No. 56 (as referred above). Contending thereof that on

2
27.07.2007 the defendants/respondents have conspired to forcefully
occupy the property, which otherwise is claimed by the
plaintiff/respondent to be belonging to them in terms of the pleading
raised in the Suit, the plaintiffs have claimed, that he had acquired the
property by way of its succession having devolved upon him from his
Late father Mr. Bhikha. It was further contended by the
plaintiff/appellant that after the death of Late Bhikha the property in
dispute lying in Khasra No. 56 having an area of 0.700 hectares stood
recorded in his favour in the revenue records by way of succession.
The case of the plaintiff/appellant was that the land in dispute was
leased to his Later father Bhikha about 42 years back, and at the time
of allotment of land it was having Khasra No. 48, which on
conclusion of survey operation it was renumbered as Khasra No. 56.
He has submitted that ever since then the plaintiff is in peaceful
possession over the same and the title stands vested in him, as he
stands recorded as sankramaniya bhumidhar over the disputed land in
the revenue records. The cause to institute the Suit as per the
plaintiff/appellant arose when on 27.07.2007 at about 8:00 AM,
defendants and his allies attempted to forcefully occupy the same by
digging foundation over the property, and when it was resisted by the
plaintiff he was maltreated by the defendants.
3. The Suit was contested by the defendants/respondents
and the written statement Paper No. 29A/1 was filed by the defendant
nos. 3 to 5 on 30.05.2011. The contest by the defendant was raised on
the ground that in fact there was no cause of action as such for the
plaintiff/appellant to institute the Suit because the so called incident of
27.07.2007 has never chanced nor there was any attempt was made by
the defendants to make any effort to forcefully occupy the so called
property claimed by the plaintiff/appellant to be belonging to him. It
was further contended that the Suit suffered from the vices of non-joinder of necessary parties because in the south of the property in
dispute the other co-tenure holder, who was the owner of Khasra No.
146 <+ having an area of 0.0200 hectares was a necessary party to have
been impleaded as a party to the Suit and, since he has not been
impleaded as party to the Suit, hence, the Suit suffered from the vices
of non-joinder of necessary parties. Defendant no. 4 contended that he

3
had purchased the property with its co-owner Sharafat Ali from its
previous owner, i.e. defendant no. 3, vide registered sale deed dated
27.07.2007 and same was registered with the Sub-Registrar.
Defendant no. 4 contended that defendant nos. 3 and 5 had been
wrongly made as party to the Suit.
4. Based on the aforesaid rival pleadings, the learned Trial
Court had framed the following issues:

5. In order to adjudicate the present second appeal, the
prime concern would be the determination made on issue nos. 1 and 2,
which related to the determination of title and ownership of the
plaintiff/appellant over the property in dispute, which was the subject
matter of the Suit, and as to who was in effective possession of the
property.
6. Based on the aforesaid pleadings raised in the plaint the
plaintiff/appellant has adduced the documentary evidences by way of
a list paper no. 8C, which included the certified copy of Khatoni paper
no. 9C, Khasra with regards to 1414 fasli as paper no. 10C, Khatoni
for fasli year 1385 to 1388, i.e. paper no. 11C and other documents in
support of their contention that they are the owner in possession in the
property in question, panariskshit khasra paper No. 13C1.
7. Apart from it, the plaintiff/appellant has also adduced the
oral testimony of PW1 Ramzan, which was placed on record by way
of an affidavit in examination as paper no. 88A2 his cross-examination as paper No. 89A2 and also adduced the evidence of
PW2, i.e. Smt. Naseema and her affidavit, i.e. paper no. 90A2. The

4
oral testimony of plaintiff/appellant witnesses were cross-examined
by the defendants, which is proved by Paper No. 91A/2.
8. The defendants in contravention to the pleading and the
evidence adduced by the parties have placed on record number of
documents through List Paper No. 32C/1including that of Khasra and
Khatoni pertaining to 1415 to 1420 fasli as paper no. 74C/1 to 74C/2
and the sale deed dated 27.07.2009 as paper No. 75C/1 to 75C1/4,
certified copy of Map Paper No. 76C/1, apart from adducing the oral
testimony of DW1, i.e. Ishaq and his affidavit as paper no. 96A2. The
defendants witnesses were cross-examined by the plaintiff/appellant.
9. Learned counsel for the appellant based upon the
substantial question of law as framed in the memorandum of appeal,
particularly has harped upon the fact that what would be the situation
in those suits where the issues thus framed pertaining to the title and
possession, if it is concurrently decided by both the courts below in
favour of the plaintiff, whether at all the suit was to be compusorily
decreed for grant of permanent injunction or despite of the said
finding having been recorded still the Suit could be dismissed at all.
10. Apparently, the argument and substantial question of law
as framed seems to be quite alluring, but the said finding is not
substantiated from the fact that if the finding, which has been recorded
by the Trial Court is taken into consideration and, particularly, the
finding, which has been recorded while adjudicating the issue nos. 1
and 2, the Court has recorded a finding to the effect that though
apparently the title and possession of the disputed property might have
been expressed to be shown to be vested in favour of the
plaintiff/appellant, but in the absence of there being any identification
of the property and its exact location no decree of permanent
injunction could be granted in favour of the plaintiff/appellant. It was
further observed that the boundaries of the disputed property and,
particularly, the south portion of the chauhaddi as shown in the map,
where it describes the Government Canal if the said property is said to
be a property belonging to the defendant no. 4 in Khasra No. 146 <+

5
having an area of 0.0200 hectares, no decree of permanent injunction
could be granted.
11. Because despite of proof of title, the plaintiff had failed
to prove in any manner that the disputed property was with the
chauhaddi of the disputed property given in the Suit, even on appraisal
of testimony of PW1 and PW2 it could not be conclusively inferred
that it lies within the boundary of disputed property. Even as per the
documentary evidence adduced by the plaintiff/appellant, there was
no such documentary evidence produced on record to show that
disputed property was the property as shown in the plaint. Rather the
Courts have held that as per defendants document, i.e. the Map Paper
No. 76C/1, it shows that the disputed property is the property, which
adjoins Khasra No. 56, i.e. exactly the property shown in the plaint
lies in Khasra No. 146, which proves that the property lying in the
south of the description of the property Government Canal is not
there, but rather its property of co-owner Sharafat Ali and defendant
no. 4.
12. On scrutiny of statement of PW1, i.e. plaintiff Ramzan
himself, who in his cross-examination has submitted that, adjoining to
his property is the property of Ishaq for whom he admits that he has
not raised any construction, rather the tin-shed is at a distance. Rather
he has explained his ignorance about the land on which the tin-shed
has been constructed. Similar was the statement of
plaintiffs/appellants witness PW2, where she has stated that the tin-shed is near the property of Ishaq, and behind the tin-shed there exist
government water canal. Thus, it was held that the property of
Ramzan, which is shown as to be on Khasra No. 56, the DW1 has no
relation to it. Thus, both Courts have held that even as per Amin's
report the tin-shed of Ishaq and Mateen is existing on Khasra No. 56,
which is near the disputed property.
13. In view of the finding recorded, the Court has held that
though there might have been a title and possession of the
plaintiff/appellant over the property in dispute, but the cause of action

6
as pleaded and with regards to the identification of the property in
relation to which the decree of injunction has been sought was not
substantiated and, established by evidence, but was rather contrary to
the plaintiff's evidence itself. Consequently, the Trial Court has
dismissed the Suit of the plaintiff/appellant. Even as per Paper No.
10C/1 dated 24.07.2007, i.e. the khasra it shows that wheat crop is
grown on disputed property, whereas PW1 and PW2 has stated that
rather 'chari' is grown, which is self contradictory. There is
contradiction in evidence and statement.
12. Based on the aforesaid judgment of the Trial Court and
the so called purported anomalies committed by it, the First Appeal
was preferred by the plaintiff/appellant being First Appeal No. 34 of
2016 'Ramzan vs. Gaffar and Others'. Learned counsel for the
appellant has drawn the attention of this court that at an appellate
stage too they have filed an application on 25.10.2017 before the
Appellate Court calling for an Amin's report in order to identify the
exact location of the property in question. The said application as
preferred by the appellant on 25.10.2017 calling for a report from the
Amin was allowed, the Amin's report was called for and,
consequently, the same was submitted on 23.12.2017, i.e. paper no.
30C/1, wherein, the Amin has opined that as far as the property in
question is concerned in the South there lies Khasra No. 57 and in the
west-Khasra No. 55 and in the east-Khasra No. 114. Hence, the
chauhaddi, which has been given in the plaint map and in accordance
with the report of the Halka Revenue Inspector, Khasra No. 56 is
shown to be of a very smaller area as per the map of the Amin dated
23.12.2017, i.e. Paper No. 30C/1/3.
13. The argument of the learned counsel for the appellant is
that as per the finding of the Amin's report has also not been
appropriately determined and considered by the learned Appellate
Court and the finding, which has been recorded in relation to the
Amin's report by the Appellate Court is contained in paragraph- 32
onwards recorded in the Appellate Court's judgment is perverse and
contrary to the Amin's report.

7
14. The Appellate Court after scrutinizing paper no. 30C/1/2
has held that as far as the disputed property Khasra No. 56 is
concerned, the property, which was shown by way of tin-shed is
existing in near about area of Khasra No. 146 and the Appellate Court
had appreciated the contents of the Amin's report paper no. 30C and
has recorded the finding that as far as the existence of the said tin-shed is concerned, which is contended to have been disputedly raised
by the defendants/respondents over the land belonging to the
plaintiff/appellant, was a fact which was not even substantiated by the
Amin's report and with regards to the said location of the said tin-shed
for which the injunction was sought.
15. The Appellate Court on scrutiny of documents and report
had held that Khasra No. 56 shown to be having an area of 0.0700
hectares, of which plaintiff is the owner, but that in itself does not
prove the existence of the tin-shed to be within Khasra No. 56, as
claimed. Glaring facts concluded by evidence are:
 (i) Tin-shed is not on Khasra No. 56 of plaintiff.
 (ii) Property not identified to be disputed even as per
Amin's report.
 (iii) No cause of action as on 27.07.2007 was existed
because the pleading is that there existed 'chari'
and 'grass', whereas Khasra Paper No. 10 C1
shows existence of wheat crop on the land.
 (iv) because PW1 Ramzan in his cross-examination
had admitted that no interference was made by
defendant over disputed land.
 (v) PW2 in her statement denied the act of digging
foundation by defendant.
15. Consequently, the judgment of the Appellate Court too
was affirmed the judgment of the Trial Court by dismissing the
Appeal on 03.08.2019.

8
16. After having heard the learned counsel for the appellant
and after scrutinizing the judgments under challenge before this Court
from view point of the substantial question of law as framed by the
learned counsel for the plaintiff/appellant in the memorandum of
appeal to the following effect, this Court is of the view that in view of
the finding of fact that once the plaintiff approaches the Court for a
grant of decree of permanent injunction even despite of having
established the fact of being the owner in possession of the property, it
still becomes all the more necessary for raising a cause of action to
institute the Suit, to show as to whether the property for which
injunction has been sought, was the construction in existence over the
property, which is being proved to be belonging to be under the
ownership of the plaintiff. Thus, the substantial question as framed
hereunder does not involve consideration to be answered:
"A. Whether a suit for injunction could have been
dismissed by the courts below after recording
concurrent finding with regard to the ownership and
possession of plaintiff?
 B. Whether the learned appellate court could have
dismissed the suit when the trial court recorded
specific finding with regard to possession of the
plaintiff which finding attained finality because of
want of challenge by the defendant and the land stood
demarcated during the pendency of appeal and the
plaintiff proved that the defendant encroached upon
during the pendency of appeal?
 C. Whether in case a defendant encroaches upon the suit
property after filing of the suit or after dismissal of the
suit during pendency of appeal, the court is powerless
to grant appropriate relief to undo the mischief
committed by the defendant after filing of the suit."
17. In such an eventuality, the interpretation given to the
Amin's report by the Appellate Court too happens to be in consonance
to the exact location of the property and even as per the oral testimony
of PW1 and PW2, which has been shown to be in the Amin's report,
which is not existing over the Khasra No. 56 having an area of 0.0700
hectares and, consequently, as far as the location of the tin-shed and
the ownership of the plaintiff/appellant over the property in question
that happens to be a concurrent findings of facts recorded by both the
courts below and substantial question of law as framed therein by the
appellant since it only relates and confines to the effect as to whether
there could be a denial of a decree of permanent injunction despite of

9
having been established to be the owner in possession of the property,
there is no such substantial question of law required to be answered in
relation to the interpretation or the impact of the Amin's report, which
it would have over the plaintiff's right to continue to occupy the
property. Because the said report is not the subject matter raised
before the Appellate Court or even before this Court that the report
was misinterpreted its finding recorded by the Appellate Court while
dismissing the appeal preferred by the plaintiff/appellant.
18. In that view of the matter, this second appeal is
concluded by concurrent finding of facts and none of the substantial
question of law as framed in the memorandum of second appeal calls
for consideration by this Court in the exercise of its jurisdiction under
Section 100 of Code of Civil Procedure.
19. Consequently, the second appeal lacks merit and is,
accordingly, dismissed.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 07.12.2019
Pooja
